title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_0RD0RA_1RE0LD_1LF---_1LA1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_0RD0RA_1RE0LD_1LF---_1LA1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A bouncer over a 1010… background (fast left side) with a slowly growing right end where defects (00, 11, longer gaps) accumulate; chaotic, open. Close relative of 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_0RD0RA_1RE1LE_1RF---_1LA1LF (part03).
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 8 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,408 cells have been visited and 18,247 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.526). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.233).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: B, C and A shift 1010↔0101 rightward, A and F cross 10/01 leftward unchanged. Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (E reading 1) needs 10100, 10101 or 10110 to the left (nearest first); any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas
claims.text: The left side is the plain 10 background of a bouncer: rightward passes in A/B/C shift every copy of 1010 to 0101 or back (proved shift rules), leftward passes in A/F leave it as it is. The left end grows like the square root of the step count.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (E reading 1) needs 10100, 10101 or 10110 to the left (nearest first); any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas
claims.text: The left side is the plain 10 background of a bouncer: rightward passes in A/B/C shift every copy of 1010 to 0101 or back (proved shift rules), leftward passes in A/F leave it as it is. The left end grows like the square root of the step count.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. E reading 1 halts. In the 5-cell closed language this needs 1010x on the left and a 1 under the head; every right window starting with 1 is allowed, so the language does not locate the halt.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 36,408 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.value: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas
html: The left side is the plain 10 background of a bouncer: rightward passes in A/B/C shift every copy of 1010 to 0101 or back (proved shift rules), leftward passes in A/F leave it as it is. The left end grows like the square root of the step count.

The right end (slow side, exponent about 0.23) is where the action is: near it the background carries defects. Written as runs of 1s (numbers) and gaps (. one 0, : two 0s, _k k 0s), the last 40 runs at step 982,617,644 are 2 . 1 . 1 . 1 : 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 _4 1 . 1 . 1 … 1 _6 1 . 1 .. Defects appear at the right wall, travel and merge; their pattern has no visible period.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: E reading 1 halts. In the 5-cell closed language this needs 1010x on the left and a 1 under the head; every right window starting with 1 is allowed, so the language does not locate the halt.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): B, C and A shift 1010↔0101 rightward, A and F cross 10/01 leftward unchanged; for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Compare with the part03 twin (one transition differs): if their right-end defect sequences coincide, the defect mechanism is in the shared states.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.526). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.233).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,408 cells (23,764 left of the start, 3,404 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
